caption: Modeled SOM distribution (fixed-seed Monte-Carlo over committed assumptions): p10 $37.6M, p50 $93.6M, p90 $226.3M. A modeled estimate, not a measured revenue figure.
Modeled LTV:CAC distribution: p10 2.56×, p50 8.47×, p90 28.2×. The wide spread reflects pre-revenue assumption uncertainty; the median clears the 3× SaaS-health line but the p10 tail does not.

Revenue multiples of graph-DB / viz / workflow / low-code comparables (n=30, median 33.0×). Each point is a public/known financing comp; MetroGraph is pre-revenue, so these bound an option value, not a mark.

The most-capitalized companies in the indexed competitive set (213 companies, 327 financing rounds). Capital concentration marks where incumbents can out-spend on the converging canvas/agent features.
Top features by customer-pain score across the feature taxonomy (110 features). High-pain canvas/visualization capabilities (≥0.8, in orange) are the whitespace the wedge targets.

The 13 wedge claims re-graded against cross-domain evidence. None exceed supported-by-proxy; every one carries pending-experimental-validation, derived from the empty MetroGraph behavioral-data tables.

How the HCI literature attaches to market/wedge claims: 82 grounding edges support, 11 contradicting edges refute (force-directed wins path-finding/subgraph tasks). The empirical floor is real but context-dependent.
Dated competitor moves by quarter; orange marks moves that erode a feature MetroGraph claims. The drumbeat on canvas + agent nodes is what fires the red-team falsifiers.

Claims with derived primary backing (green) vs proxy/secondary support (grey), by domain. Only HCI (46/49) and VoC review-mining (42/63) carry primary backing; market/product/finance are secondary by construction.
The gold layer is honest about dissent: 406 claims span supported through refuted. Refuted/disputed claims are retained and reframed as hypotheses, not deleted.

The typed relationship graph (2,091 edges, 21 types) is the algebra the synthesis layer reads: grounds/contradicts from HCI, erodes from competitive intel, gates from governance, measures from product.
Each financial driver's p10–p90 range with the p50 marker. These input ranges (not a variance decomposition) are what the Monte-Carlo propagates into the wide LTV:CAC and SOM spreads.
Open compliance gaps gating the enterprise segment, by severity. The blocker count is the honest finding for an early-stage tool — each blocker becomes a dated roadmap item.
Recommendations ranked by a derived priority score (not hand-set). Purple bars are the four needed-but-missing MetroGraph experiments — roadmap items, never assumed as done.
Integration targets ranked by derived priority (reach × strategic-fit / effort). Postgres leads on information_schema introspection and ICP reach; feasibility grades are design estimates.
